q: בן 73, מגיע למרפאה גריאטרית בשל חוסר יציבות, חולשה כללית, ונפילות חוזרות. הוא מתאר קצב הליכה איטי, מתלונן על דחיפות במתן שתן ומספר שהוא קם לשירותים 3-4 פעמים בלילה. שולל בעיות זיכרון, הזיות או מחשבות שווא. רופא המשפחה ניסה טיפול ב- DOPICAR לכמה חודשים ללא שיפור משמעותי. בבדיקה- לחץ דם בשכיבה 156/84, אך יורד ל- 104/73 סיסטולי בעמידה, דופק כ- 95. מתנייד עם הליכון, הליכה shuffling gait, תנועות רגליים ללא קואורדינציה טובה, כיפוף גב קדימה, ללא רעד במנוחה, אבל רעד בביצוע תנועה מכוונת, תנועות עיניים תקינות. בהערכה קוגניטיבית MMSE – 29/30, MRI של המוח ללא הרחבת חדרים או גרורות. איזו מהאבחנות הבאות היא הסבירה ביותר?
o: מחלת פרקינסון
Lewy Body Disease
Progressive supranuclear palsy
Multisystem Atrophy
explanation:
**Multiple system atrophy (MSA)** best fits parkinsonism with prominent autonomic failure and cerebellar findings. The shuffling gait, flexed posture, instability and falls coexist with the substantial orthostatic blood-pressure fall in the stem and urinary urgency/nocturia. Cognition is preserved; MMSE 29/30 alone does not exclude DLB, but the whole pattern supports MSA (pp. 939, 941).

**A. Parkinson disease.** Wrong, poor levodopa response together with prominent autonomic dysfunction and cerebellar findings favors an atypical parkinsonian syndrome (pp. 939, 941).
**B. Lewy body disease.** Wrong, dementia near motor onset, fluctuations in alertness and hallucinations characterize DLB. Their absence as a pattern makes it less fitting here; the MMSE alone does not exclude it (pp. 939, 941).
**C. Progressive supranuclear palsy.** Wrong, vertical gaze impairment supports PSP. Eye movements are normal in the vignette, and ataxia with marked autonomic dysfunction fits MSA better (pp. 939, 941).
**D. Multiple system atrophy.** Correct, prominent autonomic dysfunction, cerebellar signs and relatively few cognitive manifestations match MSA. Poor levodopa response also supports an atypical syndrome (pp. 939, 941).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 939, 941.

q: A woman hospitalized with acute decompensated heart failure has a reduced response to an oral diuretic. Which mechanism explains a possible advantage of intravenous administration according to Hazzard?
o: Increased drug absorption through an edematous bowel wall
Increased drug clearance caused by an edematous bowel wall
Reduced drug absorption through an edematous bowel wall
Reduced drug clearance caused by an edematous bowel wall
explanation:
**Bowel wall edema** can decrease oral diuretic absorption in acute heart failure. Intravenous administration avoids this absorption step and may therefore produce more effective diuresis (p. 1182; application of the stated mechanism). The source attributes this in part to "bowel wall edema, which may decrease the drug’s absorption." (p. 1182).

**A. Increased drug absorption through an edematous bowel wall.** Wrong, increased absorption would not explain the stated advantage; the source identifies decreased absorption through edematous bowel (p. 1182).
**B. Increased drug clearance caused by an edematous bowel wall.** Wrong, clearance is not the bowel-related mechanism described; the source identifies impaired absorption (p. 1182).
**C. Reduced drug absorption through an edematous bowel wall.** Correct, decreased absorption is the mechanism explicitly given for a possible intravenous advantage during an acute episode (p. 1182).
**D. Reduced drug clearance caused by an edematous bowel wall.** Wrong, decreased clearance is not the explanation given for bypassing oral administration; the described problem is absorption (p. 1182).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1182.

q: An 80-year-old woman is hospitalized with pneumonia and delirium. Evaluation and treatment of the causes are ongoing. Despite nonpharmacologic measures, her behavior threatens her safety and interrupts essential treatment. Which prescribing principle applies?
o: Start at a full dose to obtain a rapid, predictable response
Plan prolonged treatment to prevent later recurrence of confusion
Use the lowest starting dose for the shortest necessary duration
Treat improved agitation as evidence that the causes have resolved
explanation:
**Medication for delirium symptoms** is reserved for selected situations involving safety or interruption of needed treatment. Sedation can further cloud mental status and prolong delirium (p. 888). "Any drug should be initiated at the lowest starting dose for the shortest time possible." (p. 888).

**A. Start at a full dose to obtain a rapid, predictable response.** Wrong, a full initial dose conflicts with the stated lowest-starting-dose principle and its concern about adverse medication effects (p. 888).
**B. Plan prolonged treatment to prevent later recurrence of confusion.** Wrong, planned prolonged treatment conflicts with the shortest-possible-duration principle; sedative medication may itself prolong delirium (p. 888).
**C. Use the lowest starting dose for the shortest necessary duration.** Correct, this matches the dose and duration principle for the safety-threatening situation described (p. 888).
**D. Treat improved agitation as evidence that the causes have resolved.** Wrong, medication can obscure the course of mental-status change, so reduced agitation does not establish resolution of the causes; this is an inference from that warning (p. 888).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 888.
ref: Hazzard Ch 22 — MEDICATION PRESCRIBING AND DE-PRESCRIBING

q: בן 70, עצמאי וללא ירידה קוגניטיבית, ברקע יתר לחץ דם וסוכרת, מאוזנים, התקבל למחלקה כירורגית עקב חסימת מעיים. עלה למחלקה בשעה 23:00 בלילה לאחר שהיה של 24 שעות במחלקה לרפואה דחופה. בקבלתו באי שקט פסיכומוטורי, לא מתמצא במקום ובזמן. לפי CAM המטופל אובחן עם דליריום. הכירורגים מעוניינים לקבל הסכמה של המטופל לניתוח שיבוצע בימים הקרובים במידה ולא. ישתפר בטיפול שמרני מה הגישה המתאימה לקבלת הסכמה לניתוח למטופל זה?
o: כדאי לנסות לדבר עם המטופל בבוקר. יתכן ויהיה שיפור במצבו ויהיה כשיר לחתימה
יש למלא תעודת רופא ולמנות אפוטרופוס בן משפחה
מומלץ לבצע בדיקת MINI-COG להערכת מצבו הקוגניטיבי
מומלץ להתחיל טיפול תרופתי באנטי פסיכוטים לצורך שיפור מצבו הקוגניטיבי ואז ניתן יהיה לקבל הסכמה
explanation:
**Delirium** is acute and fluctuating. A patient's cognition may improve during the day, allowing reassessment of the ability to understand the proposed operation and make a decision during a lucid interval (Hazzard 8e, pp. 151, 883).

**A. Try speaking with him in the morning; he may improve and be able to consent.** Correct, the official answer is consistent with fluctuation. When surgery is not immediate, reassess understanding, appreciation, reasoning and expression of a choice, without promising recovery by morning (pp. 151, 883).
**B. Complete a physician's certificate and appoint a family guardian.** Wrong, appointment is by judicial order; the medical opinion forms part of the application and is not itself the appointment. Current delirium alone does not establish persistent incapacity that removes the need for reassessment (MoH procedure, pp. 2–3; Hazzard, pp. 151, 883).
**C. Perform Mini-Cog to assess cognition.** Wrong, cognitive screening alone does not assess the four abilities needed for this particular surgical decision (pp. 121, 151).
**D. Start antipsychotics to improve cognition, then obtain consent.** Wrong, the source does not show that these restore consent capacity; they are a last resort and do not replace assessment of decision-making ability (p. 889).

Capacity can fluctuate in delirium and should be reassessed during lucidity. Trying again in the morning is reasonable in this nonurgent scenario, but recovery is not guaranteed and no universal waiting rule applies (Hazzard 8e, pp. 883, 889). Respect for autonomy requires a real attempt to hear the patient when capable (p. 151).
Mini-Cog is cognitive screening, not a substitute for assessing understanding, personal appreciation, reasoning and expression of a choice about this operation (pp. 121, 151).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 121, 151, 883, 889; Israeli Ministry of Health, guardian appointment during hospitalization procedure, pp. 2–3.

q: מה כוללת גישת ה- SPIKES לבישור בשורה מרה?
o: Setting, Perception, Invitation, Knowledge, Emotions, Strategy
Surrounding, Percussion, Innovation, Keep, Examination, Suggestion
Supervision, Pain, Isolation, Kneel, Explanation, Sorry
Suggestion, Pity, Independent, Key, Extraordinary, Sufficient
explanation:
**SPIKES** structures the delivery of bad news: Setting means a private, seated conversation without interruptions; Perception checks what the patient understands; Invitation asks how much information is wanted. Knowledge means sharing information gradually in plain language; Emotions calls for an empathic response; Strategy and Summary closes with a clear plan (Hazzard 8e, p. 1102, Table 72-3).

**A. Setting, Perception, Invitation, Knowledge, Emotions, Strategy.** Correct, this sequence matches the table: prepare the meeting, establish understanding and the desire for information, share knowledge, respond empathically, and plan next steps (p. 1102).
**B. Surrounding, Percussion, Innovation, Keep, Examination, Suggestion.** Wrong, percussion, innovation, and physical examination are not the listed stages. This sequence misses the patient's understanding, information preferences, and empathic attention to emotions (p. 1102).
**C. Supervision, Pain, Isolation, Kneel, Explanation, Sorry.** Wrong, pain, isolation, and kneeling are not the table's stages. It omits checking perception and the desired extent of information and the shared plan at the end (p. 1102).
**D. Suggestion, Pity, Independent, Key, Extraordinary, Sufficient.** Wrong, pity and general words about independence and a key are not the defined process. SPIKES requires understandable information, recognition of emotions, and a clear next plan (p. 1102).

Source: Hazzard 8e, p. 1102, Table 72-3.

q: מה לא נכון בנוגע לתסמינים או הפרעות נוירופסיכיאטריות במצב של דמנציה?
o: תסמינים נוירופסיכאטרים מגיבים היטב לטיפול בתרופות אנטי-פסיכוטיות
הפרעות נוירופסיכאטריות הן הסיבה העיקרית להכנסת מטופלים הלוקים בדמנציה למוסדות
הפרעות נוירופסיכאטריות יכולות להימצא בכל שלבי הדמנציה, אפילו לפני שמאובחנת ירידה קוגניטיבית
הפרעות נוירופסיכאטריות מזרזות התקדמות של דמנציה ממצב קל למצב קשה
explanation:
The question asks for the **incorrect statement**. Antipsychotics have limited benefit and important risks for neuropsychiatric symptoms in dementia, so nonpharmacologic approaches come first (pp. 919, 927).

**A. Neuropsychiatric symptoms respond well to antipsychotic medication.** Correct, this is the false statement accepted as the answer to the negative question. The source describes modest efficacy and increased mortality and cardiovascular/cerebrovascular risks, rather than a generally good response (p. 927).
**B. Neuropsychiatric disorders are the main reason for institutionalizing patients with dementia.** Wrong, not accepted as the false statement: difficult behavior and psychosis are among the strongest determinants of institutionalization because of their impact on patients and caregivers (p. 919).
**C. Neuropsychiatric disorders can occur at every stage, even before cognitive decline is diagnosed.** Wrong, not accepted as the false statement: symptoms can occur throughout dementia and before cognitive decline, consistent with the source (p. 919).
**D. Neuropsychiatric disorders accelerate progression from mild to severe dementia.** Wrong, not accepted as the false statement: the source associates symptoms with faster progression. This is a prognostic association and does not require attributing it to a single causal mechanism (p. 919).

The accelerated-progression statement is wrong as an answer because its content is true in the sense described by the source: these symptoms are associated with faster progression, without assigning one causal mechanism (Hazzard 8e, p. 919).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 919, 927.

q: Per UK NICE guidance, which hospital patients should automatically undergo a falls risk assessment?
o: Patients aged 65 or older after a documented inpatient fall, plus all patients aged 50–64
Patients aged 65 or older with abnormal balance testing, plus those aged 50–64 after a fall
All patients aged 65 or older, plus those aged 50–64 with an underlying risk condition
Patients aged 65 or older taking psychoactive drugs, plus those aged 50–64 with an MMSE below 17
explanation:
The chapter describes automatic multifactorial assessment for hospital patients aged 65+ and at-risk patients aged 50–64 (p 637)
Patients aged 65 or older after a documented inpatient fall, plus all patients aged 50–64 — A previous inpatient fall is not required for those aged 65+, while ages 50–64 require an underlying risk condition (p 637)
Patients aged 65 or older with abnormal balance testing, plus those aged 50–64 after a fall — The older age group is assessed automatically; the younger group qualifies through an underlying risk condition (p 637)
Patients aged 65 or older taking psychoactive drugs, plus those aged 50–64 with an MMSE below 17 — Medication use and the residential-care MMSE threshold do not define the hospital eligibility rule (p 637)
